assertion.statement: For genuine isogenies of abelian surfaces, degree is multiplicative and deg([n])=n^4 for nonzero integers n.
assertion.objects: Integral denominator-cleared isogenies [m]u and their compositions with multiplication maps on abelian surfaces.
assertion.hypotheses: Characteristic zero; m,n are positive integers for which the representatives are genuine isogenies.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such integral representative and positive m,n.
assertion.parameter_range: Genuine integral isogenies only; rational quasi-isogeny degree is subsequently defined and proved well-defined.
assertion.uniformity: The same degree law holds independently of coefficient prime and is unchanged by field conjugation.
assertion.normalizations: Degree is the rank of the finite locally free map; [-1] is a degree-one automorphism.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No degree assigned to [1/m] as an algebraic morphism; no rational discrepancy or finite cochain conclusion in this source input.
assertion.limit_order: Apply the integral theorem before dividing numerical degrees by m^4.

use.reason: Apply the integral multiplication-degree theorem to the two cleared representatives at lines17–18; the following local algebra derives denominator independence and the scalar law. This source input is not that derived output.

supplier.statement: Multiplication by n on an abelian variety of dimension g has degree n^(2g), and degree of genuine isogenies is multiplicative.

publication.title: Abelian Varieties
publication.authoritative_version: Original1986 chapter with the exact degree pages inspected in the retained sign-source review
publication.locator: Theorem8.2 and preceding paragraph,p115; proof p116
publication.corrections: This is the multiplication-degree input, separate from Proposition12.9 used for the trace polynomial.
